citation: Quint, J., Zhu, P., Balu, R., Rappaport, S., & DeLaurentis, M. (2015). Scaling Up the Success for All Model of School Reform: Final Report from the Investing in Innovation (i3) Evaluation. New York, NY: MDRC.
report_number: MDRC report (Sept 2015); ERIC ED579089 (full report); ED579090 (executive summary)
design: Blocked school-level (cluster) RCT; 37 elementary schools (19 program / 18 control) in 5 districts (districts = randomization blocks / fixed effects); Success for All whole-school reading reform (a comprehensive school-reform model delivered via long-duration teacher professional development, tutoring, materials, and continuous-improvement processes from the program developer) vs business-as-usual; subject = Reading; row 93 corresponds to the AUXILIARY analysis sample = students in grades 3-5 (registry grade band 3-6) tested in spring 2014, the third implementation year. Impact estimates from a two-level HLM (students nested within schools, district fixed effects), intent-to-treat, regression-adjusted for random-assignment block and student/school covariates.
problems: The impact tables (Table 5.6) for the grade 3-5 auxiliary sample report only the standardized effect size (impact / control-group SD) and a p-value; they do NOT print the impact standard error. The report's only direct precision figures for these exact estimates are the realized Minimum Detectable Effect Sizes (Appendix Table D.2, grade x test). I back-computed impact_se in effect-size units as SE = MDES / M, using M = 2.89 (two-tailed alpha=0.05, 80% power, cluster df ~31 from 37 schools - 5 blocks - 1; the large-sample multiplier 2.80 would lower every SE by ~3%). Because MDES is reported to only 2 decimals and the exact df/multiplier MDRC used is not stated, the recorded g_se/g_var are approximate (likely accurate to ~10%); the g point estimates themselves come directly from the reported effect sizes and are reliable. The Grade-5 Gates-MacGinitie Total MDES (0.11) is anomalously small relative to its component subscales (Comprehension 0.25, Vocabulary 0.23) and the impact (0.02) -- almost certainly a table typo/rounding artifact -- so the back-computed g_se for that one record is flagged as unreliable. Per-grade n_t/n_c are taken from the table-note ranges (using the larger Gates-MacGinitie subsample n for the GM tests and the smaller-end n for the state-test rows); exact per-outcome Ns are not individually printed. No ICC is reported in the report (NOT guessed); cluster_adjusted=true because impacts come from the two-level HLM. This is row 93's only sample (grades 3-6); the report's headline/primary sample is a separate K-cohort followed to grade 2 (Tables 5.2-5.5, Woodcock-Johnson / TOWRE) which falls outside the grade 3-6 band assigned to this row and is therefore not extracted here.

effect_sizes.test_name: Gates-MacGinitie Reading Test, Comprehension subtest (scale score)
effect_sizes.g_method: Reported effect size d = impact/control-SD = 1.09/39.27 = 0.03 taken directly from Table 5.6. g = J*d, df = n_t+n_c-2 = 2839, J = 0.99974, g = 0.02999. impact_se in ES units = MDES(0.21)/2.89 = 0.0727 (Appendix Table D.2); g_se = J*0.0727 = 0.0726; g_var = g_se^2.
